intro: I’m Abhay Bhat. I’ve been around the startup ecosystem through venture capital, co-founding ChemoMicrobiome, and operator roles in biotech. Alongside that, I’ve worked across neuroscience, microbial genomics, microscopy and computational chemistry. I’m currently a Research Associate at the Long Lab at UIUC.

education.name: University of California, Berkeley
courses: Introduction to Computational Molecular & Cell Biology

timeline.title: Research Associate
timeline.place: Long Lab · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
body: Single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis across prairie and meadow voles, including quality control, ambient-background correction, doublet detection and integration.
Behavior-processing workflows for home-cage and chamber assays: event definitions, multiple-scorer summaries, disagreement reports, and exploration of automated video scoring.
timeline.lesson: A behavioral measure depends on the event definition and the person scoring it. Those choices need to be visible alongside the result.

timeline.title: Business Development Associate
body: Turned customer requirements into fermentation-program scopes, pricing, timelines and handoffs to scientific and process teams.
Coordinated proposals, CRM workflows and contracting across technical, commercial and legal stakeholders. Contributed to discussions about digital tools and fermentation data.
timeline.lesson: A scope of work is where a promising conversation becomes specific enough to execute: what gets measured, who owns the next step, and what happens if the result changes the plan.

timeline.title: Founder’s Office & Business Development Intern
body: Partner landscaping and prioritization for an oncolytic-virus platform; competitive intelligence and positioning informed by scientific literature.
Organized data-room materials and supported partnership preparation, external communications and literature-analysis workflows.
timeline.lesson: A long partner list becomes useful only when there is a reason for each organization to engage, and a specific conversation to have next.

timeline.title: Venture Analyst Fellow · second stint
body: Returned for a second period of venture research, including biotech and deep-tech company analysis, sector landscapes and investment discussions.
Across the two stints, researched technical differentiation, market structure and commercialization assumptions, drawing on literature and founder discussions.
timeline.lesson: The useful part of a memo is often the unresolved question that could change the investment view.

timeline.title: Co-founder
body: Product and business development for a microbiome-based chemotherapy-toxicity concept. Customer discovery with patients, clinicians, founders, pharma and insurance stakeholders.
Nucleate Bay Area Chapter; Emerging Leaders Award at the Nucleate Forum. Participated in UCSF NSF I-Corps; the case study documents that customer-discovery chapter.
timeline.lesson: The person who wants a result, the person who acts on it and the person who pays can require very different evidence.

timeline.title: Product Commercialization Consultant
body: Assessed the US opportunity for a diagnostic platform through stakeholder interviews, competitor and patent research, pricing and workflow analysis.
Worked with a multidisciplinary team to examine where a faster result could justify a change in the care pathway.
timeline.lesson: Assay runtime is only one part of the time between a patient arriving and someone being able to act.

timeline.title: Venture Analyst Fellow · first stint
body: First period in early-stage deep-tech venture research, contributing company notes, market landscapes and technical analysis.
timeline.lesson: Learning to separate an interesting technical result from a credible reason to build a company around it.

timeline.title: Research Associate
timeline.place: NanoOrg Lab · Indian Institute of Science
body: Worked on biological imaging and computational analysis at the Centre for Neuroscience, including fluorescence and super-resolution microscopy.
Contributed data analysis to the Arl15 collaboration; co-author on the resulting Traffic paper published in 2025.
timeline.lesson: An image-analysis result needs to stay connected to the preparation, acquisition and segmentation choices that produced it.

timeline.title: Research project
body: Project at IIT Madras in collaboration with NASA: comparative microbial genomics, genome annotation, pangenome comparisons, and SNP/InDel analysis.
Presented a research poster and supported metagenomics analysis acknowledged in the two linked publications.
timeline.lesson: Different reference genomes and comparison sets can change which differences become visible.

timeline.title: Intern
body: Worked on Python pipelines during an internship at BrainSightAI.
